text: The university presents its academic environment as a community of scholars, students, and alumni focused on learning, innovation, research, and social impact. Its stated approach combines academic excellence with practical teaching, industry interaction, international cooperation, entrepreneurship, communication skills, and opportunities for professional development.

The university website lists programmes including B.Tech CSE (AIML), B.Tech CSE (AIDS), B.Tech CSE (Cyber Security), B.Tech CSE, Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Commerce, Master of Business Administration, and M.Tech CSE Interdisciplinary Studies.

Admission Process Admission to the B.Tech program at Sanjivani University is conducted through the centralized admission process governed by the Directorate of Technical Education, Maharashtra. Candidates must have passed HSC with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as compulsory subjects. Fee Structure The annual tuition fee for the B.Tech program is revised each academic year as per the Fee Regulating Authority notification and is payable in two installments, one at the start of each semester.

Examination Rules Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each subject to be eligible to sit for the semester end examinations. Any student falling below this threshold must apply for condonation through the department office at least two weeks before the examination schedule is published. Backlog Policy Students carrying backlog subjects from previous semesters are permitted to appear for a maximum of two backlog papers alongside their current semester examinations, subject to timetable clashes being resolved by the examination cell. Revaluation Students who wish to apply for revaluation of their answer sheets must submit a written application to the examination department within seven days of the result declaration, along with the prescribed revaluation fee.

The university website reports that Fortinet partnered with Sanjivani University to establish a Fortinet Centre of Excellence on August 28, 2024. It also reports the inauguration of an IBM Centre of Excellence on January 23, 2025. These initiatives are presented as supporting cybersecurity education, industry-relevant training, real-world project experience, technological skills, industry readiness, and innovation.

Library Timings The central library at Sanjivani University is open from 8:00 AM to 9:00 PM on all working days, Monday through Saturday. On Sundays and public holidays, the library remains open from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM for reading room access only, with book issue and return services suspended. Book Borrowing Policy Undergraduate students may borrow up to three books at a time for a period of fourteen days. Postgraduate students and research scholars may borrow up to five books for a period of thirty days.

Course Contents UNIT I Foundations of Research 9 hrs. Foundations of Research: Meaning, Objectives, Motivation, Utility. Concept of theory, empiricism, deductive and inductive theory. Characteristics of scientific method – Understanding the language of research – Concept, Construct, Definition, Variable. Research Process Problem Identification & Formulation – Research Question – Investigation Question – Measurement Issues – Hypothesis – Qualities of a good Hypothesis –Null Hypothesis & Alternative Hypothesis. Hypothesis Testing – Logic & Importance, Introduction to Systematic Literature Review (SLR), Literature review techniques (PRISMA, Scopus search), UNIT II Research Design 9 hrs. Research Design: Concept and Importance in Research – Features of a good research design – Exploratory Research Design – concept, types and uses, Descriptive Research Designs – concept, types and uses. Experimental Design: Concept of Independent & Dependent variables. Qualitative and Quantitative Research: Qualitative research – Quantitative research – Concept of measurement, causality, generalization, replication. Merging the two approaches,

and uses. Experimental Design: Concept of Independent & Dependent variables. Qualitative and Quantitative Research: Qualitative research – Quantitative research – Concept of measurement, causality, generalization, replication. Merging the two approaches, Design thinking in research, AI experiment design (train-test-validation split), Reproducibility concepts. UNIT III Measurement 9 hrs. Concept of measurement– what is measured? Problems in measurement in research – Validity and Reliability. Levels of measurement – Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio. Sampling: Concepts of Statistical Population, Sample, Sampling Frame, Sampling Error, Sample Size, Non Response. Characteristics of a good sample. Probability Sample – Simple Random Sample, Systematic Sample, Stratified Random Sample & Multi-stage sampling. Determining size of the sample – Practical considerations in sampling and sample size, Feature engineering basics, Data collection ethics (AI datasets), Bias in datasets. UNIT IV Data Analysis 9 hrs.
